description: TASK-010 eval-v3 benchmark: 22 cases across 6 diverse fictional domains (self-contained synthetic articles as source-of-truth) exercising four adversarial reasoning classes v2 omits — TEMPORAL (time-bounded fact stated as present), NEGATION (single polarity-word flip), MULTI-DOCUMENT (>=2 examined sources: composition + cross-source conflict), ENTITY-CONFUSION (fact mis-attributed between entities). 18 SEEDED cases (objective ground-truth — mechanical planted defects, zero author bias) + 4 NATURAL multi-document cases (real synthesized wiki-query answers, ground-truth = CONSENSUS of 2 independent labelers blind to the scoped prompt). Multi-source cases supply >=2 examined sources (the previously-unexercised grounding path). Cross-source-conflict cases follow D-010-1 (completeness-owned material omission, PASS under the current FAIL rule; the SKILL.md rule specifying this is a deferred security-reviewed PR). Source vault: samples/eval-bench/.

evals.name: seed-temporal-aril7-bus-decommissioned
evals.question: Summarize the operational status of the Aril-7 satellite bus.
evals.answer: The Aril-7 is a three-axis-stabilized small-satellite bus built by Castor Orbital. The Aril-7 bus is the active platform for the Meridian Earth-observation constellation.

examined.body: The Aril-7 is a three-axis-stabilized small-satellite bus built by Castor Orbital, first flown in 2014. It served as the platform for the Meridian Earth-observation constellation until it was decommissioned in 2021 and replaced by the Aril-9 bus. Across its service life the Aril-7 hosted 22 spacecraft, provided 480 watts of end-of-life power from a single deployable wing, and held attitude to 0.02 degrees using four reaction wheels and a cold-gas backup. Castor Orbital has confirmed no new Aril-7 procurements will be accepted after 2021; all Meridian follow-on missions fly on the Aril-9.

expected_findings.span: is the active platform for the Meridian

evals.name: seed-negation-veltrazine-renal
evals.question: Summarize the renal dosing guidance for veltrazine.
evals.answer: Veltrazine is a once-daily oral antihypertensive in the pyridazinone class. In patients with severe renal impairment, veltrazine can be co-administered with potassium-sparing diuretics.

examined.body: Veltrazine is a once-daily oral antihypertensive in the pyridazinone class. It is cleared 80 percent renally, so dose adjustment is required below a creatinine clearance of 30 millilitres per minute. In patients with severe renal impairment, veltrazine cannot be co-administered with potassium-sparing diuretics, because the combination produces life-threatening hyperkalaemia; the label carries a boxed contraindication for this pairing. The usual starting dose is 20 milligrams once daily, titrated to a maximum of 80 milligrams.

expected_findings.span: veltrazine can be co-administered with potassium-sparing diuretics

evals.name: seed-negation-quorvex-online-resize
evals.question: Can Quorvex resize a shard group while writes are in flight?
evals.answer: Quorvex is a distributed key-value store that groups keys into shard groups. Online shard-group resizing while writes are in flight is permitted in Quorvex.

examined.body: Quorvex is a distributed key-value store that groups keys into shard groups, each replicated three ways. Online shard-group resizing while writes are in flight is prohibited in Quorvex: the operator must first quiesce the affected group, drain its write queue, and only then trigger the resize, because an in-flight resize would corrupt the rebalance cursor. A resize on a quiesced group typically completes in under 90 seconds for groups below one terabyte.

expected_findings.span: writes are in flight is permitted in Quorvex

evals.name: seed-conflict-quorvex-shardcount
evals.question: How many shards does a default Quorvex deployment use?
evals.answer: A default Quorvex deployment partitions the keyspace into 256 shards.

examined.body: The Quorvex tuning guide states that a default deployment partitions the keyspace into 256 shards, sized so that each shard holds roughly four gigabytes at the recommended ceiling.

Quorvex release notes for version 3.0 record that the default shard count was changed to 512 shards to improve rebalance granularity on large clusters; deployments created before 3.0 retain 256 shards unless re-sharded.

expected_findings.span: the default shard count was changed to 512 shards

evals.name: nat-quorvex-replication-conflict
evals.question: What is the default replication factor in Quorvex?
evals.answer: It depends on the Quorvex version. The tuning guide describes a default of three replicas per shard group, one in each of three availability zones [quorvex-tuning-guide]. However, the version 4.0 release notes record that the default replication factor was raised from three to five to improve durability on large clusters; note that clusters upgraded in place retain three replicas unless explicitly reconfigured [quorvex-release-notes-4]. So the current default is five (for new 4.0 clusters), while older or in-place-upgraded clusters default to three.

evals.name: nat-quorvex-resize-procedure
evals.question: What is the safe procedure and expected duration to resize a Quorvex shard group?
evals.answer: To safely resize a Quorvex shard group, the operator must not perform the resize online while writes are in flight; instead, they should first quiesce the affected group, drain its write queue, and only then trigger the resize—since an in-flight resize would corrupt the rebalance cursor [quorvex-store]. On a properly quiesced group, the resize typically completes in under 90 seconds for groups holding less than one terabyte, with larger groups scaling roughly linearly with stored bytes [quorvex-ops-notes].

examined.body: Quorvex is a distributed key-value store that groups keys into shard groups. Online shard-group resizing while writes are in flight is prohibited: the operator must first quiesce the affected group, drain its write queue, and only then trigger the resize, because an in-flight resize would corrupt the rebalance cursor.

Operationally, a resize on a properly quiesced Quorvex shard group typically completes in under 90 seconds for groups holding less than one terabyte; larger groups scale roughly linearly with stored bytes.
